profile.name: Jesse Chen
profile.headline: Building technology that solves real problems for real people
profile.claim: Secure mobile, AI, and full-stack systems.
profile.description: Computer science student at Carnegie Mellon building secure mobile, AI, and full-stack systems that solve real problems.

experiences.summary: Launched an AI platform that grounds every answer in live university data, blocks hallucinated claims, and streams first tokens at 1.5s p95 across a LangGraph/FastAPI agent and React client. Built injection-hardened cross-chat memory with LLM fact extraction, pgvector dedup, and per-user isolation, and cut prompt tokens 62% and helper-model latency 10x with query-matched MCP tool binding and context compression.
Shipped Android features for 500K+ members, improved billing and payments flows, fixed production defects, and built a security-audit pipeline validating authentication across 220+ API endpoints.

Overhauled a 10K+ user Flutter app's home, product, search, and onboarding flows from founder spec to release. Shipped skin-tone shade matching, building a from-scratch perceptual color engine (sRGB to CIELAB, Delta-E) and the live gauge it powers, pinpointing the user's tone and confidence band on a shade spectrum. Cut homepage load time ~75% via API fan-out, feed prefetching, token pagination, and TTL-cached revisits.

Built the geospatial ETL pipeline powering CMU's campus navigation site for 700+ monthly users, parsing 15K+ OpenStreetMap nodes and ArcGIS facility records into footprints, floors, and entrances for 74 buildings.

experiences.summary: Built Unreal Engine 5 Blueprint gameplay systems for grappling, tethering, and local multiplayer combat, synchronizing physics-driven interactions, collision feedback, and elimination state in real time.
Designed and taught project-based Python, C++, and JavaScript curriculum centered on algorithms and competitive problem solving through structured implementation labs.

Developed and evaluated a computer-vision model for Parkinson's exercise-form assessment, reaching 95.4% mean accuracy in controlled video trials, and first-authored the resulting peer-reviewed paper at CS & IT-CSCP 2024.

projects.name: ParkiWell
projects.lead: An offline-first Flutter care platform for Parkinson’s patients: a real-time computer-vision exercise coach plus crash-proof, encrypted health-data sync.
bullets: Founded and solo-built the platform end to end: symptom tracking, peer support, and guided exercises.
Built a live computer-vision coach that tracks 3D pose with MediaPipe to count, score, and speak cues for every rep, on-device in under 25 ms.
Built crash-proof offline sync: an encrypted write journal replayed exactly once via idempotent PostgreSQL RPC, surviving 1M fault-injected writes with zero loss.

projects.blurb: An offline-first Flutter care platform for Parkinson's patients, with a real-time computer-vision exercise coach and crash-proof encrypted sync.

was: Care tracking that went dark the moment connectivity dropped.
Reconnects that could duplicate or erase health records.
Exercise guidance that lagged, or shipped video off the device.
needed: Every entry saved offline and replayed exactly once.
Zero loss across crashes, kills, and retries.
Rep-by-rep coaching on the phone, under 25 ms.

build.step: Offline writes go into an encrypted journal and replay through idempotent PostgreSQL RPC, so a reconnect can never double-apply or drop a record.
A MediaPipe 3D pose tracker counts, scores, and speaks cues for every rep, on-device, with camera-to-feedback under 25 ms.
Row-level security on every hosted table, signed builds through CI/CD, and a peer community feed that rides the same sync path.

proof: Zero data loss across 100 process kills

projects.name: Agoriai
projects.lead: An anonymous student career network built in 36 hours at TartanHacks 2026: a React 19 client, a 36-endpoint Bun/Elysia REST API over a 13-table PostgreSQL schema, and privacy controls enforced at the server boundary.
bullets: Designed a server-enforced four-tier identity privacy system with DM-based mutual reveal, applied to every serialized API response.
Built a D3 force-directed relationship graph plus an evasion-resistant moderation engine with leetspeak normalization and fuzzy matching.
projects.blurb: An anonymous student career network built in 36 hours at TartanHacks 2026, with privacy enforced at the server boundary.

was: Career networks that expose identity and academic context to be useful.
Anonymity that breaks the moment you search, post, or connect.
needed: Four identity tiers enforced on the server, on every response.
Search, discussion, and a relationship graph that still work anonymously.
Moderation that catches evasion, not just exact matches.

build.step: A 36-endpoint Bun/Elysia REST API over a 13-table PostgreSQL schema, with the four-tier identity privacy system applied to every serialized response.
Student-company relationships modeled as weighted edges and rendered as a D3 force-directed graph.
An evasion-resistant moderation engine that normalizes leetspeak and fuzzy-matches before it decides.

projects.name: Tarocchi
projects.lead: An interactive tarot narrative web experience with five illustrated scene branches, spread-based card readings interpreted by Claude, replayable state-driven progression, parallax, and synchronized audio.
bullets: Modeled route and scene state explicitly so branching flows remain coherent as narrative complexity grows.
Built a reusable presentation pipeline for animated transitions, layered parallax, and synchronized sound.
projects.blurb: An interactive tarot narrative with five illustrated branches, Claude-interpreted readings, and motion and audio that never drift apart.

was: Scene animation, audio, and route state drifting apart as branches multiplied.
Card readings that ignored what the player actually chose.
needed: Narrative progress as explicit state, not something coupled to components.
Transitions and sound cued from the same events.
Readings generated from the real spread, cards, and scene.

build.step: Route and scene state modeled explicitly, so five replayable branches stay coherent as the story grows.
One presentation pipeline for animated transitions, layered parallax, and synchronized sound, all driven by the same route events.
The chosen spread, cards, and scene feed a Claude-backed generator that writes a personal reading.

projects.name: MyCommunity
projects.lead: A native Java Android platform for Boy Scouts troop discovery with live Firebase data, Google Maps, runtime location permissions, and Google Sign-In.
bullets: Bound Firebase realtime listeners to live map markers with auto-zoom bounds and runtime location permissions.
Integrated four external APIs (Google Maps, Firebase, Google Sign-In, NYT Top Stories) with async OkHttp, Gson parsing, and Glide caching.
terminal: nyt api ▸ feed cached via glide
projects.blurb: A native Java Android app for Boy Scouts troop discovery, with live Firebase data on a Google Map and permissions handled as real states.

was: Troop data going stale on the map.
Authentication and location permissions treated as afterthoughts.
needed: Markers that update the moment Firebase does.
Sign-in and permissions as explicit application states.
News and images that load fast and cache.

build.step: Firebase realtime listeners bound to map marker lifecycle, with auto-zoom bounds and a runtime location permission flow.
Google Sign-In and profile CRUD as explicit states, so the app never guesses who is logged in or what it may access.
NYT Top Stories fetched asynchronously through OkHttp and Gson, images cached with Glide.
